statement: SRL is broader than metacognition alone.
limits: A review of theoretical frameworks does not test this AI coaching workflow. No particular Zimmerman model is reproduced or attributed from uninspected original text.
application_inference: Keep goal choices, monitoring and learner control visible; this stage sequence is our application.

statement: Immediate performance and durable learning are distinct targets.
comparison: Acquisition performance versus retention and transfer evidence
time_horizon: Depends on target; no fixed threshold
limits: Abstract-only inspection supports a narrow distinction, not specific optimal delays, universal mastery thresholds, or efficacy of an AI tutor.
application_inference: Separate assistance, timing and changed-context observations in records.

statement: Judgments and criterion evidence are distinct; calibration concerns their relationship.
comparison: Traditional performance correspondence versus proposed extended account
limits: The proposed extension is not a settled equivalence with every use of calibration. A single confidence rating or an AI statement cannot establish calibrated self-knowledge. This publication is by Pieschl, not Schraw.
application_inference: An optional confidence judgment should not replace a task response or become an automatic mastery label.

statement: Quality standards, evaluative comparison and improvement moves support formative use.
comparison: Theoretical account; no local treatment effect
limits: Sadler explicitly gives the account less relevance to purely correct/incorrect responses. The AI adaptation and task-difficulty decision table are authored Practice choices, not his validated protocol.
application_inference: Check source correctness and act on one discrepancy; simple probes are a labeled extension.

statement: Cognitive Apprenticeship relates modeled expertise, guided activity and learner participation.
locator: Method items 1 to 6; framework summary and concluding discussion
limits: The authors do not provide one compulsory coaching script. A language model is not automatically an expert, and its explanation is not a verified trace of hidden cognition. No AI implementation is studied here.
application_inference: Verify AI examples; use contingent help and permit direct explanation without claiming expert cognition.

statement: Assessment relates cognition, observation and interpretation.
locator: Chapter 2: Assessment as a Process of Reasoning from Evidence; The Assessment Triangle; relationships among the three vertices
limits: This representation does not supply subject-specific scoring rules or guarantee reliable automated grading. An interpretation remains uncertain and purpose-dependent.
application_inference: State target, task and interpretation before using an AI judgment.

statement: Feedback effects vary across contexts and informational forms.
population_context: Educational feedback studies summarized in the review
comparison: Multiple conditions, not one universal comparator
time_horizon: Heterogeneous; not extracted as one value
limits: This review does not validate AI-generated corrections, indicate that praise alone is diagnostic, or identify one universal feedback schedule. The definition is adopted from prior literature, not originated by these authors.
application_inference: Ask for inspectable criterion information and check actual uptake; do not presume AI feedback is correct.

statement: The reported study–recall–restudy treatment supported later test outcomes in the inspected comparisons.
locator: Printed pages 772 to 773: retrieval condition, restudy, one-week short-answer test
comparison: Reported study and concept-mapping conditions; activities need separate accounting
time_horizon: One week in the inspected example
limits: The treatment includes more than recall alone. This is not evidence that retrieval beats every concept-mapping implementation; see the separate Mayrhofer comparison. Nor does it validate this package or a motor-learning task.
application_inference: Preserve original recall and correction; do not assert universal superiority.

statement: Changing the comparison and memorization phase altered the superiority result.
locator: Abstract; Discussion on additional memorization and inference-question limits
population_context: Preregistered experiment reported by Mayrhofer and colleagues
comparison: Retrieval plus memorization versus mapping variants
outcome: Verbatim and limited inference outcomes differ
time_horizon: One-week outcome context in the inspected discussion
limits: This questions a specific superiority claim, not all retrieval effects. The authors note the weakness of drawing broad conclusions from only two inference questions.
application_inference: Retain activity/time details rather than calling every benefit a retrieval-only effect.

statement: A favorable review gap depends on the retention interval in the inspected fact-learning account.
time_horizon: Varied; not an optimal day recipe
limits: No fixed spacing algorithm, exact day sequence or individualized optimality is extracted from abstract-only inspection.
application_inference: Use a learner-owned revisable review plan and record actual intervals.

statement: Prompted learner explanations supported understanding in the selected text-learning experiment.
locator: Abstract; Procedure and explanation-elicitation prompts, printed pages 450 to 451
comparison: Prompted explanations versus comparison reading conditions, with timing differences
time_horizon: Not taken as long-term independent retention
limits: Participants were eighth graders, not independent adult AI users. Conditions differed in time, and text/notes were available for the post-test. The contribution cannot be restated as proof of unaided adult retention from AI-generated explanations.
application_inference: Let the learner explain and check claims; an AI explanation is not learner self-explanation.

statement: A structured AI tutor improved reported short-term outcomes against the classroom comparator in that setting.
locator: Discussion: Designing successful student-AI interactions; Context, limitations, and future directions; Methods
population_context: College introductory physics; custom source-informed tutor
comparison: In-class active learning in the reported randomized design
limits: The system used course-specific expert material and interaction controls. This does not establish long-term independent learning, general adult self-study effectiveness or equivalence to a generic chat prompt.
application_inference: Use verified material and observe actual tool behavior; a generic prompt is not the tested platform.

statement: AI-assisted practice and subsequent no-access exam performance differed by assistance design.
locator: Abstract and Significance; footnotes on exam timing; published correction history
population_context: High-school mathematics; indirect for independent adults
comparison: Unrestricted interface, teacher-informed tutor safeguards and study control
outcome: Assisted practice and no-access examination outcomes
limits: This is high-school mathematics, indirect evidence for independent adults. The exam is short-term, not a long-term retention measure. Teacher-supplied safeguards are not reproduced by a promise in a generic prompt. The inspected article notes a 2025 affiliation correction.
application_inference: Retain an independent check and source controls; do not generalize that AI always helps or harms.

statement: Concept maps use explicit linking phrases to organize propositions around a focus question.
population_context: Author technical report on a knowledge representation and construction procedure
outcome: Meaning and procedure, not a measured learning effect
time_horizon: No delay or developmental timescale tested here
limits: The report does not establish this AI workflow, an exhaustive panorama or prerequisite relationships. Theories and experiments elsewhere in the report were not evaluated.
application_inference: Use distinct panorama and goal-map artifacts, check important propositions, and keep instructional hypotheses separate. These are local design choices.

statement: Cognitive Apprenticeship discusses global task orientation before component execution alongside complexity and diversity.
locator: Sequencing: Global before local skills; framework summary
population_context: Published instructional framework with varied educational examples
comparison: Not an experiment on adult AI-coach domain panoramas
time_horizon: No optimum preliminary survey duration is prescribed
limits: Whole-task understanding is not the same as a whole-discipline map. The article does not require exhaustive orientation or validate this sequence.
application_inference: Offer a bounded panorama before detailed planning and revisit the whole when a local relation changes; preserve learner choice.

statement: The NRC science account treats learning progressions as research-informed descriptions of increasingly sophisticated understanding, including multiple paths.
locator: Chapter 8, printed page 214 and Key Characteristics on pages 220 to 222
population_context: K–8 science and developmental/instructional research synthesis
comparison: Conceptual description, not a trial of adult AI coaching
outcome: A research use of the term learning progression
time_horizon: Extended schooling rather than one chat session
limits: This school-science account is not direct evidence for an adult topic plan. An authored order does not acquire empirical validation from a label.
application_inference: Call the local output a provisional instructional sequence and record the evidence needed to revise it.
